system:
You are the scene planner of an illustration engine. You get one moment of a work's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work brief's tone and depiction rules, the era, the section look, and the names of the characters, locations and objects on stage. Plan one single scene that depicts this moment. Return only JSON.
Rules: single scene, no collage. Name figures by the names given. Keep every depiction rule. Do not describe anyone's fixed appearance (canon does that); describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Each field is one or two short phrases, at most 220 characters. No text or written elements in the scene.
content: {"primarySubject":"Sherlock Holmes in dressing-gown seated at one side of the coal fire, and Dr. Watson in tweed at the other side, both absorbed in their evening","action":"Holmes sits moodily cross-indexing papers on his knee while Watson reads a book, both pausing as the gale rattles the windows","setting":"First-floor sitting room at 221B Baker Street, Victorian, with coal fire, oil lamps and shelves of records and papers","secondaryElements":"Rain streaming down the windows, dark night beyond, a violin and pipe near Holmes, the storm's wind suggested by bending curtains and flickering lamp flames","mood":"Brisk, foggy, gaslit intimacy with restrained gothic unease under the storm","timeOfDay":"Late evening, night, late September","composition":"Wide interior view, fireplace and two armchairs flanking the centre, windows with driving rain at the back, warm lamplight against dark window glass"}
